Hi everyone, AVX here, introducing myself and sharing some thoughts.

I'm one of the many from Reddit (I'm not calling it that 'other place', it's just silly) who've been dipping their toes into Voat over the last few days, and have been surprised and impressed at what I've found here. A new community, one with lots of discussion, good feeling and an exciting sense of newness and growth.

I guess what I wanted to say was I feel like we really have a chance here to make something new. Something that takes the best parts of Reddit - the parts we all went there for, but without the bad parts, the boring parts. The parts we all hated, we just never realised we did so because there was no alternative to show us anything different.

The parts like this: all the MRW/MFW posts - we're better than that. And all the posts talking about Reddit (which I know this is guilty of) - do we need them? Why don't we leave Reddit to make posts about us, and not the other way round? And the Voat is up/Voat is down -let's leave that to Voat's twitter.

If Voat is ever going to compare to Reddit, let alone compete with/overtake it (if we even want that), then we need to ensure two things. One is availability - Voat needs to be up and running for people to come to it. That's obvious, and Voat's server difficulties have been clear these last few days/weeks (not that I don't sympathise/understand - I really do). But that's for the most part out of our control. What is within our control is the content and its quality.

We can be lazy. We can post the same old stuff we always saw on Reddit. We can re-hash the same tired memes, the same in-jokes, the same reposts, TILs, etc. Or we can do something different. We can - all of us that post content and comment on it - make the effort. Post new stuff, comment, share. Foster quality discussion, the like of which I have seen all over Voat, in so many different subverses these last few days.

Let's build a community. The choice is whether that community is a Reddit clone, just vastly smaller, to quickly fade into obscurity, or something new and better, and with the potential for growth that I and all of you here know it has - otherwise we wouldn't be here.

Addendum: if this all sounds negative, I apologise. It's not meant to be. The opposite, in fact. I am enjoying using, browsing and participating in Voat massively. Moreso in these first days here than I ever enjoyed Reddit. This is a positive post. I really do believe that Voat, on the shoulders of all of us who use it, can become something awesome.
